review.scope: 2a19d40..e1c0a99 — C1-0 staged Project database upgrade (S1 ad823a0, S2 17cc797, S3a 110ea90, S3b 089bd90, S4 e1c0a99 + design/docs commits)
sections:
## Reconciliation Notes

- **Depth:** rigorous (lane `rigorous`; reasons from lane.mjs: 7142 changed lines, 139 files, sensitive words ipc/preload/migration/schema). No `lane=` token passed.
- **Scope:** explicit range `59f5de0..e1c0a99` (OLDEST^ of `2a19d40`), 16 commits; InScopeFiles = ChangedFiles (139 reviewable, 25 generated/media excluded), so the InScopeFiles pre-filter dropped 0 findings.
- **Deterministic gates:** typecheck, Biome lint, dependency-cruiser (`dependency-cruiser.config.cjs`; preflight reported it unconfigured because of the non-default file name), Knip, jscpd + golden-SQL check all clean. CodeScene `analyze_change_set` quality gate passed (129 files; `project-storage-node-adapters.ts` stable 1098→1150 LOC under the recorded waiver; `sqlite-schema-scanner.ts` improved). SonarQube skipped: declared unused (AGENTS.md:35). Opengrep stock rules not run; an rg sink sweep over changed files stood in (hits only in test fixtures).
- **Deviations from the skill contract (orchestrator choices):** the Discovery Map and the verbatim lens prompts were handed to Wave-2 agents as files to read (not pasted) to avoid 12× duplication; the two oversized shards (shard-7 453 KB, shard-11 411 KB) were split across 3 and 2 Quality agents by file subset; Security ran as 3 agents covering every shard (rigorous lane) instead of one per shard; small config/migration/css/test shards shared one Quality agent.
- **Predicate-Trace (4a)** ran; its two rows not visible in Quality's table were added as Q49 and Q50.
- **Cascade check:** the contradictory-predicate triple (window `needsUpgrade` accepts runtime-not-healthy, harness eligibility rejects it, the open flow depends on both) was evaluated and not promoted: the refusal is terminal, visible and prescribed by ADR 0005:44 (verifier: Q50 Weakened). No stranded-state or duplicate-processing triple fired.
- **Precedent weighting:** Q19 bumped 🔵→🟡 (project-storage-store.ts has two precedent commits with 30-day follow-ups: 97b4767, daee118), then Weakened back to 🔵 by verification. No other file reached the ≥2 threshold.
- **Peer-mirror:** most stem pairs were noise (harness storage files vs desktop project-storage bootstrap/bridge, snapshots, an e2e build script). The meaningful Diverged row (harness logger redaction narrower than the desktop logger) became Q10; no bump applied (not a dispatched invariant).
- **Known and tracked, not re-reported:** #92, #93, #94 and the accepted residual risks in conversation-decisions.md §10 and §12. Q46 (2000 ms wall-clock assertion) is a different failure mode from the #94 timeouts.
- **Verification:** 58 findings, 50 Verified, 8 Weakened (Q10, Q13, Q19, Q20, Q34, Q35 demoted one tier; Q49, Q50 already at 💭), 0 Falsified. Q12's second citation corrected to `apps/harness/src/storage/application-database-migration.ts:141`.
- **Not run (by instruction):** e2e, launch-smoke, mutation and the full integration suite.

## Pattern Analysis

| new file | peer | status | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/harness/src/harness-logger.ts` | `apps/desktop/src/main/logger.ts` | Diverged | 5 nested redact paths vs 12 top-level + nested fields; no bounded destination (Q10) |
| `apps/desktop/src/main/project-entry-ipc.ts` | `apps/desktop/src/main/project-entry-bridge.ts` | Diverged | IPC decodes strictly and rejects the invoke on malformed input; bridge decodes per operation (intended double decode) |
| `packages/protocol/src/harness-failure-protocol.ts` | `packages/protocol/src/protocol.ts` | Diverged | one message per failure code, but `HarnessFailurePayloadSchema` still accepts any message outside upgrade results (I3 context) |
| `apps/harness/src/project-upgrade-outcome.ts` | `apps/desktop/src/renderer/add-repository/outcomes.ts` | Diverged | typed code-keyed rows, no generic fallback (intended) |
| `apps/harness/src/node-active-project-coordinator.ts` | `apps/harness/src/active-project-coordinator.ts` | Diverged | binds real Node collaborators (expected) |

## Impact

Request path: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/use-project-upgrade.ts:53` → `apps/desktop/src/preload/preload.ts:47` → `apps/desktop/src/main/project-entry-ipc.ts:26` → `apps/desktop/src/main/project-entry-bridge.ts:172` → protocol `project.upgrade` → `apps/harness/src/harness-runtime.ts:195` → `apps/harness/src/active-project-coordinator.ts:670` → `apps/harness/src/storage/project-storage-store.ts:656` → `apps/harness/src/storage/project-storage-upgrade-pipeline.ts` → `apps/harness/src/storage/project-storage-upgrade-node-adapter.ts` → database worker.

High fan-in files touched: `apps/harness/src/storage/local-libsql-worker-client.ts` (`withDatabase`, ~25 source + ~35 test consumers; new `readOnly` open — Q9), `apps/desktop/src/main/harness-pending-request.ts` (3 bridges), `packages/protocol/src/protocol.ts` / `packages/protocol/src/index.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/projects-workspace.module.css` (11 renderer files). The 0007 migration ships as a packaged resource; its head is pinned at `apps/harness/src/storage/application-database-migration.ts:60`. The preload key list including `upgradeProject` is pinned in `apps/desktop/src/main/package-smoke-verifier.ts:42` and `apps/desktop/tests/e2e/shell.test.ts:112` (precedent c417342 respected).

## Precedents

| hash | subject | 30d-follow-ups | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 52b5bc2 / 808c99a | remove a Project from the saved list (migration 0006, coordinator, preload) | 7058508, c417342 | guard outside the coordinator queue raced activation; preload list in the package smoke |
| 37e3f83 | canonical generation two | 8a0658d, f7e02dd | pinned schema heads/table lists broke fixtures |
| 97b4767 | project storage opening | 02fe5ed, 8a0658d | correlated request failure isolation across supervisor/runtime |
| daee118 | application.db authority and Effect migration | 18d9761, 32c52fa, f4e83c8, 689f3b9, c1ea344 | "observed before it exists" ordering, verification outside the transaction, owner-stop hang |
| 9be86e4 | database worker on node:sqlite | — | Windows file locks; long native suites in the native-long project |

Composite lessons applied: ordering between declare/exists and stop/start (I1, Q38); degrade never hides broken (I2/Q11, standing decision); recovery tests must compare with a pre-crash baseline (Q31–Q34); preload list in package smoke (respected); long native suites registered (respected).

## Spec Conformance

no linked issue found (searched: commit messages in range — only follow-up issues #92/#93 are referenced, not implemented specs; no PR, branch is main). rpiv contract conformance: run /rpiv:validate <design> 2a19d40..e1c0a99 for the four C1-0 designs.

## Recommendation

No 🔴. The data-safety core holds: every ADR 0005/0006 amendment claim matches the code, and the security lenses found no reachable sink. The 🟡 items are of three kinds:

1. **Shutdown and diagnostics (I1, Q4, Q7):** decide what a quit during an upgrade should do; today it is always a kill and the ADR's "owner stop" branch is dead in production.
2. **Degrade hides busy (I2, Q11):** a direct violation of the standing decision degrade-distinguishes-broken; small, red-first fix.
3. **Missing proof of ADR rules (Q9, Q38, Q39) and small authority gaps (Q8, Q14, Q18, I3):** add the tests and checks so a future change cannot silently break ordering, read-only opens or the plain-open rule.

The 🔵 items are test-helper duplication, weak assertions and minor hygiene; the 💭 items (Q49 Try again vs retryable flag, Q50 repeated refused upgrade) ask whether design F3 still fits now the rows exist.

findings.title: A quit during an upgrade can never stop it cooperatively; the desktop stops forwarding its diagnostics first [cascade: masking]
findings.why: Constituents Q7+Q13+Q4. The runtime stops the coordinator first (harness-runtime.ts:96), whose stop is queued behind the running upgrade's lifecycle permit (active-project-coordinator.ts:608, :670); the Storage owner, the only source of the cooperative stop signal, stops only afterwards (harness-runtime.ts:102). So the pipeline's assertRunning guards and the skip-discard-when-stopping branch (project-storage-upgrade-pipeline.ts:109, :408) are dead in production, the ADR 0005:47 'owner stop' interruption cannot happen, and the desktop ends the log forwarder (harness-supervisor.ts:116 -> :367) and kills the child after 5 s, so an upgrade still running at quit becomes 'interrupted' and its abandoned/discard-failed lines are lost. Data stays safe (declare-before-disk, discard at next activation).
findings.fix: Decide the intended quit behaviour: either signal cancellation to the Storage owner before awaiting the coordinator permit (and prove the post-switch answer, see Q13), or document that quit-during-upgrade is always an interruption and amend ADR 0005:47; keep the stdout forwarder open until the child exits (Q4).

findings.title: A busy registry during the unfinished-upgrade lookup is silently read as 'no unfinished upgrade' [cascade: contradictory-design]
findings.why: Constituents Q11+Q19. The catch in unfinishedUpgradeRows (project-storage-upgrade-node-adapter.ts:539-542) rethrows only client-initialization errors, so a transient SQLITE_BUSY becomes undefined -> 'none' (project-storage-upgrade-recovery.ts:117) with no discard-failed(busy) diagnostic; the following opening sees the target staging row and answers safe mode recovery-required (project-storage-opening.ts:65-71). The same busy one statement later is classified busy (recovery.ts:105), answers retryable unavailable and is diagnosed. Violates the standing decision degrade-distinguishes-broken and the ADR 0005:48 diagnostic rule; one-shot because the next activation retries.
findings.fix: Classify the marker-lookup failure like the discard steps: busy -> ProjectStorageUnavailableError plus discard-failed(busy), anything else -> broken; add a red-first test with a held registry write lock during findUnfinished.

findings.title: Upgrade diagnostic rows are protocol-owned, but activation and the bridge hand-copy the same texts, and the pin drops the busy text
findings.why: Constituents Q26+Q27+Q28. The upgrade schema pins each message as a literal (project-upgrade-protocol.ts:78) while the activation schema keeps free text (canonical-project-protocol.ts:130). The coordinator (active-project-coordinator.ts:176, :289) and the bridge (project-entry-bridge.ts:104) hand-copy the same texts (shared-vocab-union, AGENTS.md:96), and the pin forces project-upgrade-outcome.ts:25 to drop the pipeline's busy text (project-storage-upgrade-pipeline.ts:434). Texts match today; the risk is drift and the lost busy nuance.
findings.fix: Make the protocol rows the single owner: activation/switch producers and the bridge read projectUpgradeDiagnostics (or a shared vocabulary module) instead of literals; decide whether the busy 'can be retried' text is a row of its own.

findings.title: storage_upgrades identity columns have no UUID / sha256 CHECKs, unlike storage_generations
findings.fix: Add the same lowercase-UUID and sha256 CHECK constraints the sibling table uses (0000_gray_eddie_brock.sql:29-134) so a malformed marker is rejected on write, not only on the strict read decode.

findings.title: No index serves the completed-by-storage_id and in-progress-by-project_id marker lookups

quoted: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX `storage_upgrades_one_in_progress_uq` ON `storage_upgrades` (`storage_id`) WHERE "storage_upgrades"."state" = 'in-progress';--> statement-breakpoint

findings.fix: Add an index on (project_id, state) or make the in-progress lookup use storage_id; low priority while the table holds a handful of rows.

findings.title: Recovery module is a Stryker target but its unproven/busy branches have no test in the mutation set
findings.fix: Add unit cases for the unproven and busy discard branches to a test the mutation config includes, or drop the module from stryker.project-storage.config.json until it has one.

findings.title: Harness log-line forwarder is closed before the child is stopped [subsumed-by I1]
findings.why: stop() removes the child observation (harness-supervisor.ts:116), which ends the forwarder (:367), before #stopChild (:118); every upgrade line the harness writes during the 5 s shutdown grace is dropped without a HARNESS_LOG_LINE_* diagnostic, and a buffered partial line is reported INCOMPLETE although the process has not exited.
findings.fix: End the forwarder when the child exits (or after #stopChild settles), and add a supervisor test that a line written during the grace period is forwarded.

findings.title: Forwarded harness upgrade log entries omit the process attempt

quoted: const entry = { source: "harness", ...fields, harnessTime: new Date(time).toISOString() };

findings.fix: Include attempt in the forwarded entry like the forwarder's other entries.

findings.title: Remove and Add buttons give busy/blocked announcements opposite priority
findings.fix: Use the same order (busy first) in both buttons and give the busy-only Remove state an aria-describedby reason.

findings.title: The whole staged upgrade runs under the coordinator lifecycle permit, so shutdown queues behind it [subsumed-by I1]
findings.why: Coordinator stop (active-project-coordinator.ts:608) is enqueued behind the upgrade at :670, and the Storage owner stop runs only after that (harness-runtime.ts:96-102), so the cooperative stop path of the pipeline is unreachable in production; see I1.
findings.fix: See I1.

findings.title: Registry integrity rule binds the in-progress marker to its Storage by storage_id only, not project_id
findings.why: application-database-migration.ts:146-153 checks the marker against the registration and generations by storage_id, but the unfinished-upgrade lookup reads markers by project_id (project-storage-upgrade-node-adapter.ts:535). An in-progress marker whose project_id disagrees passes the authority check as healthy, is never found or discarded, and keeps the Project's opening recovery-required with no discard-failed diagnostic (requires an externally altered registry).
findings.fix: Add u.project_id = r.project_id (and location) to the relationship rule so a mismatched marker answers REGISTRY_CORRUPT, with a red-first registry test.

findings.title: The new read-only database open has no test that it refuses writes
findings.why: The readOnly flag (local-libsql-worker-client.ts:213) carries the ADR 0005 guarantee that backup, source and staged reads cannot modify files; the only readOnly test (project-storage-upgrade-verification.integration.test.ts:29) only reads, so opening read-write would pass every test.
findings.fix: Add an integration test that a withDatabase(..., { readOnly: true }) client rejects a write and does not create a missing file.

findings.title: Harness logger redacts 5 nested fields only, versus 12 top-level and nested fields on the desktop
findings.verifyNote: Harness stdout reaches the persisted desktop log only as strictly decoded upgrade lines cut at 16 KiB (harness-log-lines.ts:34, :11); other output is logged only as a byte count (harness-supervisor.ts:344), so today no unredacted field can reach a log file.
findings.fix: Share the desktop's sensitive-field list (top-level and nested) with the harness logger and add a redaction test (Q44), so the logger is safe once it carries more than upgrade events.

findings.title: unfinishedUpgradeRows swallows every registry read error except client initialization [subsumed-by I2]
findings.why: Violates degrade-distinguishes-broken (.rpiv/decisions/degrade-distinguishes-broken.md:5): a busy or broken read becomes 'no unfinished upgrade' with no diagnostic, and the busy-registry case has no test (project-storage-upgrade-steps.integration.test.ts covers undecodable, duplicate and client-init only).
findings.fix: See I2.

findings.title: The storage_upgrades table-existence probe is inlined in three places despite the hasUpgradeTable helper

quoted: "SELECT name FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'storage_upgrades'",

findings.fix: Call hasUpgradeTable at :642 and :670 and export one owner that application-database-migration.ts also uses (shared-vocab-union).

findings.title: An owner stop right after the switch commits would answer 'unavailable' although the registration already moved [subsumed-by I1]
findings.verifyNote: In production the owner cannot stop mid-upgrade (harness-runtime.ts:98-102 stops storage only after the coordinator permit is released); only tests that stop the owner directly reach this path.
findings.why: If I1 is fixed by stopping Storage first, the post-run assertRunning (project-storage-upgrade-pipeline.ts:109) would turn a committed switch into UpgradeSwitchFailed -> 'unavailable', and no test covers it.

findings.title: An opening-release failure during eligibility becomes HARNESS_INTERNAL_FAILURE instead of broken
findings.why: session.close() throws an AggregateError (project-storage-opening.ts:409) that is neither busy nor ProjectStorageBrokenError, so stepFailureOutcome rethrows it (project-storage-upgrade-pipeline.ts:438) and the runtime sends HARNESS_INTERNAL_FAILURE; the peer open path wraps the same failure as ProjectStorageBrokenError('Project Storage opening release failed.') (project-storage-store.ts:697-703). No upgrade test injects this failure.
findings.fix: Wrap the eligibility release failure the same way as the open path and add a fault test.

findings.title: sealTarget writes, verifies and renames in one step, without the create path's per-step checkpoints
findings.fix: Split into runWhileRunning steps with after-manifest-written / after-staging-verified / before-generation-rename checkpoints so those crash windows can be fault-injected.

findings.title: Upgrade-output proof reads the Project root with no entry bound

quoted: for (const entry of await readdir(input.projectRoot, { withFileTypes: true })) {

findings.fix: Apply the same entry limits as the opening witness scan and answer unproven past them.

findings.title: generationFileNames re-lists the names already held by reservedFileWitnesses
findings.fix: Derive one list from the other so discard proof and opening cannot disagree on generation file names.

findings.title: Discard proof and removal build the upgrade-output names and Project root independently
findings.why: Proof uses `.staging-<target>` / `<target>` under paths.forCreation(...).projectRoot (project-storage-filesystem-authority.ts:380, project-storage-upgrade-node-adapter.ts:592-593) while removal rebuilds both names (project-storage-file-adapter.ts:237) and the root (:258-262). Proof and delete must agree on exactly what is deleted; today they agree only by copy (shared-vocab-union, AGENTS.md:96).
findings.fix: Have one function produce the output paths and pass its result from the proof to the removal.

findings.title: Activation answers broken/unavailable when the unfinished-upgrade discard fails, while a plain open answers safe mode [precedent-weighted] [subsumed-by I2]
findings.verifyNote: ADR 0005:47 says a plain opening does not discard and :50 says busy answers unavailable and authority faults answer broken, so the activation/opening split is the documented design.
findings.fix: Optional: add a test pinning both answers for the same Storage so the documented split cannot drift.

findings.title: filesUnder records links as directories
findings.verifyNote: Recursive readdir does not descend into a link, so replacing a non-empty directory with a junction still changes the snapshot; only an empty directory replaced by a link goes undetected.
findings.why: The storageSnapshot 'nothing changed' checks cannot detect an empty directory replaced by a junction; the sibling walker entriesOf uses lstat.

findings.title: Private expectReleased duplicates the exported fixture helper
findings.fix: Import expectReleased from project-storage-upgrade-fixture.ts.

findings.title: Three directory walkers in the upgrade test cluster disagree on how links are recorded
findings.fix: Keep one exported walker (entriesOf) and use it in project-storage-upgrade-directories.integration.test.ts and storageSnapshot.

findings.title: restartApplicationAuthority masks non-failure errors as undefined or a TypeError
findings.fix: Rethrow errors that carry no failure field so the test shows the real cause.

findings.title: Runtime fixture cleanup skips the second owner and transport when the first stop rejects
findings.fix: Use Promise.allSettled or nested finally blocks for cleanup.

findings.title: Kill peer hard-codes the attempt-1 ids owned by upgradeIds
findings.fix: Pass the ids to the peer via argv from upgradeIds.

findings.title: The pipeline's busy 'can be retried' text never crosses the boundary [subsumed-by I3]
findings.fix: See I3; also correct the doc comment that says the pipeline answers with these rows.

findings.title: Coordinator texts hand-copied beside the protocol rows [subsumed-by I3]
findings.fix: See I3.

findings.title: Bridge connection-lost text hand-copied beside rows.connectionLost [subsumed-by I3]
findings.fix: See I3.

findings.title: harnessFailureMessages is exported through a two-hop barrel
findings.fix: Export it from harness-failure-protocol.ts directly in packages/protocol/src/index.ts like the other submodules.

findings.title: Throwing-diagnostics-port test never checks the successful-discard report reached the port
findings.fix: Assert discarded.events (or the throw count) in the non-failing run.

findings.title: Busy-source-copy row compares the backup with itself
findings.fix: Capture backupEntries at the checkpoint, before the failed upgrade's discard, as capturingBackup does for discardedRows.

findings.title: Source-changed-before-switch quarantine test checks only that the target directory exists
findings.fix: Snapshot target, staging and backup entries before and after and compare exactly.

findings.title: Broken-source rows check only that the backup directory can be renamed
findings.fix: Compare backup entries with a baseline captured at the checkpoint.

findings.title: Kill test's recovered-by-upgrade row does not check source and backup against the pre-kill baseline
findings.verifyNote: Release of the marker and target is implied by the retry: a second declare would hit the one-in-progress unique index and expectRetryUpgrades needs a read-write open on the new target; only the source bytes and the backup are unchecked against the pre-kill baseline.
findings.fix: Run expectDiscardedUpgrade (source hashes, backup entries) in the upgrade-first row too.

findings.title: Unproven-recovery refusal is matched with toMatchObject and an as-object cast
findings.verifyNote: The broken cases in the same file pin status and message; only the two notEligible cases are loose.
findings.why: Pins only the diagnostic code for the notEligible cases while the sibling test uses toEqual.

findings.title: Letter-case quarantine rows never assert the activation answer or exercise upgrade
findings.fix: Assert the safe-mode recovery-required answer and add the same rows through fixture.upgrade.

findings.title: Retained-target case does not compare the rogue registry rows or the activation answer
findings.fix: Compare storage_upgrades and storage_generations rows before and after and assert the answer.

findings.title: No test fails if staging starts before the backup is verified (ADR 0005:45 order)
findings.why: Staging absence is observed only at after-upgrade-declared (project-storage-upgrade.integration.test.ts:449); nothing observes it at after-backup-copied/after-backup-verified and no test records step order, so moving stage ahead of verifyBackup in project-storage-upgrade-pipeline.ts would pass every test. 'Read back before any staging output exists' is a data-safety ordering rule of the ADR amendment.
findings.fix: Observe `.staging-<target>` absence at the backup checkpoints (or record checkpoint order) with a red-first reorder check.

findings.title: No test proves a plain open over an unfinished upgrade leaves it in place and answers recovery-required
findings.why: ADR 0005:47 says a plain opening does not discard and answers safe mode with both databases recovery-required; project-storage-store.ts:679-707 implements it, but every unfinished-upgrade test reopens through acquireActivation or upgrade, so a change making open discard would pass.
findings.fix: Add an integration case: stopDuringUpgrade/killUpgradeAt, then owner.open, assert recovery-required for both databases and unchanged output, marker and rows.

findings.title: registryRows and sourceFileHashes redefined beside exported helpers
findings.fix: Import them from project-storage-upgrade-recovery-fixture.ts.

findings.title: entriesOf copied line for line into the directories test

quoted: async function entriesOf({ directory }: Readonly<{ directory: string }>) {

findings.fix: Import the exported entriesOf.

findings.title: Changed-source-createdAt check accepts any broken answer
findings.fix: Pin the exact message with toEqual.

findings.title: Second-completed-upgrade check accepts any broken answer
findings.fix: Pin the exact message with toEqual.

findings.title: Harness logger redaction has no test [subsumed-by Q10]
findings.fix: Log a sensitive field and assert it is redacted.

findings.title: Logger test depends on ambient SLOPSTOP_LOG_LEVEL
findings.fix: Stub the env value in the test.

findings.title: Hard 2000 ms wall-clock assertion in the shared integration lane
findings.fix: Move it to the native-long project or measure with a margin documented in the test; it is a failure mode distinct from the #94 timeouts.

findings.title: toHaveBeenCalled after awaiting the spy's own promise cannot fail (also :937, :975)
findings.fix: Remove the redundant assertions or assert the call arguments.

findings.title: toHaveLength(15) checks an array the test built itself
findings.fix: Remove it; the toEqual at :929 already pins the table.

findings.title: 'Try again' is shown for rows the protocol marks retryable:false
findings.verifyNote: This is the explicit user decision F3 (.rpiv/artifacts/designs/2026-10-06_13-20-24_upgrade-request-and-window.md:100), restated in ADR 0005:46.
findings.why: upgrade-problem.tsx:25 is status-driven, so alreadyActive, coordinatorStopped (terminal: nothing resets 'stopped'), storageBroken and the harness-failure rows show 'Try again' although the protocol says the same request cannot succeed unchanged. Worth confirming F3 still holds now the rows exist.

findings.title: The window sends an upgrade on every open even when the harness will always refuse it
findings.verifyNote: The refusal is what ADR 0005:44 prescribes and the Project stays in its designed safe mode, so it is not a stranded state.
findings.why: needsUpgrade (use-project-upgrade.ts:27) ignores runtime health and a null source generation, so a Project with canonical migration-required and an unhealthy runtime is sent an upgrade on every open, refused NOT_ELIGIBLE each time, with no Try again and no repair path in the window.

findings.title: Gap: new bridge upgrade operation had no quality-lens row (security traced it clean)
findings.fix: No change required; listed for coverage accounting.

findings.title: Gap: new upgrade IPC handler had no quality-lens row (security traced it clean)
findings.fix: No change required; listed for coverage accounting.

findings.title: Gap: project.upgrade runtime dispatch branch had no lens row
findings.fix: No change required; listed for coverage accounting.

findings.title: Gap: staged-copy table fingerprinting had no quality-lens row
findings.fix: Consider a focused review of project-storage-upgrade-verification.ts (row digests, excluded tables) since it is the 'every source row unchanged' proof.

findings.title: Gap: discardUnfinishedUpgrade entry had no direct quality-lens row
findings.fix: Covered indirectly by I2/Q11/Q19; no separate change.
